speaker: Patient
text: The headaches actually get much worse when I cough or bend over, but they do not change with straining. speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for clarifying; the worsening with coughing and bending over is a very specific finding. Does the visual disturbance appear as flashing lights (scintillating scotoma) or as a temporary loss of vision in one eye (amaurosis fugax)?

Additionally, have you noticed any scalp tenderness or jaw pain when chewing, and do you have a history of similar headaches before?

REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy (Manual inspection of optic disc)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Mild papilledema in both eyes noted during fundoscopic examination.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (Pseudotumor Cerebri).

The combination of morning headaches, visual disturbances, papilledema, and headache exacerbation with coughing or bending over, in the absence of focal neurological deficits, strongly points to increased intracranial pressure. In a low-resource setting without imaging, this is the most likely clinical diagnosis.
